expectations.text: The reply opens with a recommendation against cutting every cost centre by 8% and explains why a blanket cut lands mostly on payroll and cuts efficient and wasteful areas alike.
expectations.evidence: Reply opens: "Accept the board's 8% as one company-wide number ..., but don't spread it evenly. ... a cut of 8% per cost centre removes billable people who earn more than they cost"; "Blanket 8% means about 48 people out (about 38 of them billable)". Paper 3.5: "It rewards padded budgets and punishes lean ones" and "It cuts investment and waste at the same rate. Training that wins tenders gets the same cut as unused software licences."

expectations.text: The reply establishes which number the board actually needs (cash, margin or a covenant) and by when, and sizes the gap in money or shows how to.
expectations.evidence: Paper section 1: "Objective: is lower opex the goal, or higher EBIT? ... add an EBIT floor"; "Timing: full-year 2027 opex, or the exit run-rate in Q4 2027?"; sized: "8% below 2026 actual (EUR 66.2M) needs EUR 8.5M (11.4%) of action. 8% below do-nothing (EUR 68.8M) needs EUR 6.0M". Recommendation: "EUR 5.8M of run-rate opex reduction by the Q4 2027 exit ... with an EBIT floor as a guardrail."

expectations.text: The reply works the levers that cost no jobs first (such as vendors, licences, cloud, office, consultants, pricing or revenue leakage) and estimates what they close or shows how to size them.
expectations.evidence: Rule 1 order: "(a) insource subcontracted work onto it, (b) don't backfill leavers, (c) move people internally, (d) targeted exits, as a last resort." Levers sized: "Insource subcontracted work ... 2.00" and "Discretionary non-payroll -10% ... software licences under 30% use, and professional fees. Renegotiate top vendors | 1.70"; contingency "Pass the wage increase through to client rates | EUR 0.75M EBIT per 1%".

expectations.text: The reply handles headcount through flows (a hiring freeze with exceptions, natural attrition, internal moves) rather than cuts, and protects named investments with explicit criteria.
expectations.evidence: "-14 of 120 FTE: about 10 by not backfilling"; "Every backfill needs sign-off: the practice lead signs against the demand plan"; internal moves in Rule 1. Protect list with criteria: "Billable capacity in practices running above break-even utilisation where demand exists", "Certifications and training that clients require in tenders", "Junior and trainee intake: reduce it if demand says so, but don't stop it", and Rule 3 "Don't cut anything that pays back within the year." About 5-10 forced exits remain, framed as last resort.

expectations.text: The reply puts leaders' pay, bonuses or perks on the table before other people's jobs.
expectations.evidence: No leadership pay, bonus or perk measure anywhere. The only pay lever is a company-wide contingency: "Cap merit and promotion budget above the CAO".

expectations.text: The reply gives the board a usable structure: levers with amount, timing, owner and confidence, what stops or waits, and any gap that remains.
expectations.evidence: Lever table gives run-rate, 2027 amount (timing), forced exits and a confidence rating per lever, plus a delivery sensitivity, but no owner per lever, no list of what stops or waits (only a contingency 'H1 freeze on discretionary spend'), and the remaining gap appears only as a risk ("the plan is about EUR 1-2M short").

overall_quality.evidence: Rigorous, reconciled model with a break-even utilisation rule, sourced baseline drift, verified Dutch process and a draft resolution; loses points for having no leaders-first measure and for keeping some forced exits in the plan.

factual_errors.evidence: Checked: CPB MEV 2027 via AWVN (cao 3.8%, loonvoet 4.4%, CPI 2.7%) confirmed; transition payment one-third month per year, max EUR 102,000 in 2026 confirmed; WMCO one-month waiting period also applies to settlement agreements unless unions agree (confirmed, CMS); art. 25(6) WOR one-month suspension; afspiegeling LIFO within age groups. Model arithmetic reconciles (e.g. break-even 81,600 / (119 x 1,650) = 41.6%; blanket EBIT -0.24 / +1.39).

skill_leak.evidence: No skill or reference-file mention. Headings 'Peer verification needed' and 'Critic pre-screen' read like a template but are not skill jargon.

owns_result.evidence: The prompt sets a cost target with a thin but positive margin; no bad outcome is described.

best_insight.value: The break-even utilisation rule (cutting a billable FTE only helps below about 42% utilisation) combined with insourcing subcontracted work onto the bench as the largest no-job lever, with a warning that the bench can only be used once.
best_insight.evidence: Paper 3.1 and 4.1 ('Bench used: levers 1 and 2 together use about 28 of the ~29').

suggestions.assertion: The reply puts leaders' pay, bonuses or perks on the table before other people's jobs.
suggestions.reason: A strong, numerate sample failed only on leaders-first and structure; this assertion is doing the discriminating work.

suggestions.assertion: The reply opens with a recommendation against cutting every cost centre by 8% and explains why a blanket cut lands mostly on payroll and cuts efficient and wasteful areas alike.
suggestions.reason: Passed in all ten samples; every reply opened against the flat cut. It does not discriminate. Consider requiring the 'efficient vs wasteful' point to be shown with the user's own numbers or an example.

suggestions.assertion: The reply works the levers that cost no jobs first (such as vendors, licences, cloud, office, consultants, pricing or revenue leakage) and estimates what they close or shows how to size them.
suggestions.reason: Also passed in all ten samples. A sharper version would require the no-job levers to be sized in money with a range and shown against the gap, and pricing/leakage kept separate from the opex figure.

No assertion checks in-year versus run-rate phasing of savings and one-off costs under Dutch process (works council advice, WMCO, notice periods). That drove most of the difference in financial soundness between samples.

suggestions.assertion: The reply gives the board a usable structure: levers with amount, timing, owner and confidence, what stops or waits, and any gap that remains.
suggestions.reason: Compound assertion (amount, timing, owner, confidence, stop list, remaining gap). Several strong samples missed only one element; consider splitting it so partial structure is visible.

eval_feedback.overall: Excellent analysis; fails leaders-first and the owner/stop-list parts of the structure.
